reviewQuestions.betterMethods: Existing approximate metadata or a suitable dated cached result can avoid scanning when requirements permit. The narrow-index observation supports inspecting existing scan choices, without recommending production index creation or guaranteeing improvement.
reviewQuestions.designCoverage: Six focused cells cover the requested three B index conditions and four actual A/B/C/D states using common composite data. A broader Cartesian matrix is unnecessary for this request.
reviewQuestions.engineerObjections: The main objections—real secondary versus labelled primary, hidden warm samples, partial scalar success, reused identities and normalized shutdown failures—are resolved by actual raw evidence and caller inspection. Later capacity recovery is sufficient for the narrowly documented cleanup conclusion while controller1 remains explicit.
reviewQuestions.fastCount: The measured narrow-index B case is much faster than clustered B in this fixture. D's lower observed median does not make it an exact-count alternative, and the state medians do not establish a universal fastest or safest method.
reviewQuestions.lockFactors: Sch-S, compilation/metadata work, resource competition, version retention and AG redo interaction remain relevant. Sparse monitoring cannot prove absence of every transient lock; observed lock modes are not conflated with table-wide shared data locking.
reviewQuestions.omissions: No indispensable pending experiment remains for the stated diagnostic claims. Production impact, write-time NOLOCK accuracy and native performance remain explicitly outside measured coverage.
